findings.description: The inline user policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", allowing the service user to read/modify any EC2 instance, S3 bucket, Lambda function, or CloudWatch data in the account. Combined with long-lived access keys, compromise of this user leads to broad account takeover.

A permanent IAM access key is created for a highly privileged user with no PGP key specified, so the secret is stored in plaintext in the Terraform state file and never rotated. Anyone with state access obtains admin-level credentials.
No pgp_key argument is set, so `encrypted_secret` will be empty and the raw `secret` attribute is persisted unencrypted in state, exposing the credential to any state reader.
The output `svc_deploy_key_material` exports the access key secret material and is not marked sensitive, so it is printed to the console and stored in plan/apply logs and CI output where it can leak.

A long-lived IAM user with static keys is used for deployment automation rather than an assumable IAM role with short-lived credentials; force_destroy = true also silently deletes attached keys/MFA devices, masking credential cleanup and encouraging static key usage.
